key_insight: Tuning chloride vacancies through precursor ratios enables forming-free, gradual resistive switching in lead-free KCuCl3-x memristors for neuromorphic learning, rather than solar-cell applications.
engineering_relevance: Precursor-ratio control offers a materials-design strategy for balancing ionic mobility and defect controllability in analog synaptic devices.
method: Synthesize KCuCl3-x thin films using wet chemistry with varied precursor ratios.
Correlate chloride-vacancy concentration with electronic structure and W/KCuCl3-x/FTO memristor switching.
Use measured conductance characteristics as synaptic weights in artificial neural network simulations.
evidence_signal: At an optimal vacancy concentration of approximately 1.3 × 10^21 cm^-3, devices showed highly linear potentiation/depression and pulse endurance exceeding 10^4 cycles; simulations achieved 98.96% MNIST and 91.82% Fashion-MNIST accuracy.
watch_item: Recognition results come from simulations using measured device characteristics, not a demonstrated hardware neural network; array-scale variability and energy consumption remain unreported in the abstract.
paper_title: Precursor Ratio-Controlled Chloride Vacancies in Lead-Free KCuCl3-x Memristors for Forming-Free Gradual Resistive Switching and Neuromorphic Learning
